title: Delegation
description: AGNAP extension to GNAP. A parent agent requests authority for a child by signing a delegation assertion with the key its own access token is bound to. Separate runtime evidence proves that the parent runtime started the child runtime and binds the child key. The child presents both in a normal grant request. The authorization server verifies them, requires the child's authority to be contained in the parent's, and returns a signed receipt. Types only in milestone 1; nothing here is processed yet. The root of this schema is the union of the four artefacts so that generators emit every definition; wire messages reference the definitions directly.

DelegationRef.title: DelegationRef
DelegationRef.description: A stable, opaque identifier for one node in a delegation tree. It survives token rotation, which the token value hash does not. The authorization server issues it and callers treat it as opaque.

DelegationEnvelope.title: DelegationEnvelope
DelegationEnvelope.description: AGNAP extension. Carried in the `delegation` field of a grant request. The assertion is a compact JWS whose payload is `DelegationAssertionClaims`, signed with the parent's bound key.

DelegationAssertionClaims.title: DelegationAssertionClaims
DelegationAssertionClaims.description: Payload of the assertion a parent signs to request authority for a child. The assertion does not prove a spawn event; matching trusted runtime evidence does. Verified by the authorization server in the order: aud, iat and exp; jti is checked for prior use and recorded atomically; parent_ref resolves to an active token whose bound key produced the signature and whose value hash matches parent_token_hash when present; child_key_thumbprint equals both the requesting key and runtime evidence; the runtime evidence names the runtime bound to the parent; depth is below the policy maximum; child expiry is within the parent's; requested access and ceilings are contained in the parent's. A wider child is always denied and must begin a separately authorized root lineage.

parent_token_hash.description: Optional evidence that the parent held the token value when it signed. Not used for lookup because it changes on rotation.

child_key_thumbprint.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the child's public key. The child generates its own key pair; the parent only ever sees the public half.

aud.description: The grant endpoint of the authorization server that issued the parent token.

exp.description: Short lived. The assertion is single use; exp bounds how long the jti must be remembered.

DelegationReceipt.title: DelegationReceipt
DelegationReceipt.description: Signed by the authorization server after a child grant is issued. Returned in the grant response and available through introspection. A verifier that trusts the authorization server's key can check the lineage of any token without calling back.

DelegationPolicy.title: DelegationPolicy
DelegationPolicy.description: Set by the owner or trusted organizational policy in the server-side root authorization context. It is never accepted as authoritative from an agent. Automatic mode permits a strictly contained child grant without a new owner interaction. Manual mode requires owner interaction for every child grant. A wider child is always rejected; newly approved additional authority starts a separate root lineage.

mode.description: In automatic mode, the authorization server can issue a contained child grant without a new owner interaction. In manual mode, it must obtain owner approval for every child grant. An agent cannot approve its own request.
